articles.title: Kentucky woman indicted on charges she damaged the World War II Memorial in Washington
articles.summary: A Kentucky woman has been indicted by a federal grand jury on charges that she intentionally damaged the World War II Memorial on the National Mall in Washington, D.C. Melissa Farris is scheduled to be arraigned next week on two felony counts

articles.title: Kentucky woman indicted on charges related to World War II Memorial damage
articles.summary: Melissa Farris is scheduled to be arraigned next week on two felony counts. Grand jurors indicted her Thursday on charges of destroying the veterans' memorial and destroying government property.

articles.title: Fed will have "work to do" if inflation doesn't fade, Warsh says
articles.summary: Fed chief Kevin Warsh said in a closely watched speech that inflation remains a concern, while praising the broader U.S. economy.

articles.title: U.S. targets Egyptian bank's UAE branches under new push for Iran's economic isolation
articles.summary: Under a new rule proposed Friday by the Treasury Department, the Emirati branches of Banque Misr, Egypt's second-largest bank, would be severed from access to the U.S. financial system.

articles.title: Washington chemical tank was called unfit for service before deadly failure, investigators find
articles.summary: The U.S. Chemical Safety Board's update about the May 26 failure in Longview, which expelled enough caustic liquid to blow out building walls, is part of an ongoing investigation. The federal agency said it is still determining the cause of the failure.

articles.title: Trump to mark 9/11 25th anniversary at Pentagon
articles.summary: President Donald Trump plans to observe the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attacks at the Pentagon in Washington, D.C.

articles.title: Trump loses again in bid to erase his hush money conviction
articles.summary: It is the third time Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein has blocked Trump from having the U.S. District Court in Manhattan seize control of the case from the New York court where he was tried and convicted.

articles.title: Norway's crown prince becomes King Haakon VIII after his father's death
articles.summary: Crown Prince Haakon, 53, became King Haakon VIII when his father, Harald V, died Friday at 89. Haakon adopted the motto, "All for Norway," that dates back to his great-grandfather.

articles.title: David Booth pioneered index investing. Here's his advice for investors.
articles.summary: David Booth, the founder of Dimensional Fund Advisors, says the key to investing — and life — is to stay calm in the face of uncertainty.

articles.title: Judge says Pentagon's measures against Anthropic were 'illegal and baseless'
articles.summary: A federal judge has ruled in favor of artificial intelligence company Anthropic in its legal battle against the Pentagon after the government labeled the company as a supply chain risk earlier this year.

articles.title: Marine One has communication issue with air traffic control for second time in a month
articles.summary: The pilots of the Marine One helicopter and air traffic controllers at Ronald Reagan National Airport had difficulties communicating with each other.

articles.title: Walmart settles opioid lawsuit brought by Justice Department
articles.summary: Walmart settled claims that it filled thousands of invalid prescriptions at its pharmacies at the height of the opioid epidemic.

articles.title: Judge again blocks Trump mail ballot executive order in ruling that's likely to be swiftly appealed
articles.summary: A federal judge on Thursday halted — at least for now — attempts to implement President Donald Trump's executive order limiting mail voting.

articles.title: Younger workers are more scared of AI than older employees, survey finds
articles.summary: Employee attitudes toward AI are closely tied to their age and generational concerns, according to Glassdoor.

articles.title: Lindsay Clancy verdict: Retired judge explains what happens if insanity defense prevails
articles.summary: Lindsay Clancy could spend as few as several years in a mental institution if jurors accept her insanity defense, a retired Massachusetts judge says.

articles.title: Fed's Kevin Warsh warns inflation is too high, sparking bets rate hikes are coming
articles.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated his commitment to fighting inflation in a major speech — raising expectations that rate hikes may be coming, though he did not clearly spell out a path going forward.

articles.title: CDC: Cyclospora outbreak linked to 20 states
articles.summary: The cyclospora outbreak in lettuce has spread to 20 states, adding Georgia, Tennessee and Texas, the CDC reported. It added 528 cases.

articles.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
articles.summary: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that will help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

articles.title: ICE deports Venezuelan father from Texas to West Africa
articles.summary: Carlos Tellez Sanchez had worked at a car dealership in Dallas during the day and drove for Uber Eats at night to support his family.

articles.title: The micro-wedding trend isn't going away
articles.summary: As wedding costs skyrocket, engaged couples are eager to save. Some are turning to micro weddings to tie the knot.

articles.title: WATCH: Trump bestows Artemis II crew with Congressional Space Medal of Honor
articles.summary: President Donald Trump presented the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to the three Americans and one Canadian whose April lunar flyby set a new distance record for humanity.

articles.title: ICE officer charged in Minneapolis shooting released in Texas after judge declines to intervene
articles.summary: Christian Castro, an ICE officer charged in connection with a shooting in Minnesota, was released from lock up in Texas after a judge declined a temporary restraining order.

articles.title: Good Good Golf's very bad, bad week amid backlash over Callaway ad
articles.summary: Good Good Golf will no longer sponsor an upcoming PGA tournament, while Callaway said it has ended its partnership with the company.

articles.title: ICE awards $16.7 million no-bid contract for shock gloves
articles.summary: ICE has awarded a $16.7 million no-bid contract to the company Compliant Technologies for 6,000 shock gloves to be used to detain people by force.
